findings.problem: The process environment is unconditionally cleared and replaced with plan["environment"] immediately before importing Jupyter/pyzmq and spawning local kernels. On the required Windows host this function never asserts a process floor (SYSTEMROOT/WINDIR/PATHEXT/TEMP/PATH). The docstring claims inherited settings are stripped here, but this is a blind replace with no check and no distinction between a missing Windows floor and missing Jupyter packages.
findings.concrete_failure: If the plan env is a curated whitelist that omits SYSTEMROOT/WINDIR, import or kernel CreateProcess fails with WinError/socket/ssl/DLL errors, or ImportError is reported as dependencies_missing. Python/R kernels then never run even though ServerApp may bind.
findings.repair: After update, require a Windows floor (inject from the OS only those names if absent; never copy back credential/gateway vars). If PATH/SYSTEMROOT are still missing, _fail a dedicated code before IsolatedServerApp.initialize. Keep the Jupyter ImportError path only for real missing packages.
findings.acceptance_test: On Windows, call run_jupyter with plan.environment containing Python/Jupyter paths but not SYSTEMROOT or WINDIR: process must _fail before app.start(), not die inside zmq/tornado/Popen. Repeat with SYSTEMROOT, WINDIR, PATHEXT, TEMP, and PATH present: initialize succeeds and an approved absolute-argv python kernel Popen starts.

findings.problem: Unapproved kernel names and on-disk argv/env/metadata mismatch use the same _fail helper as startup aborts (dependencies_missing, jupyter_security_contract). That is a service-wide abort on a per-request kernelspec lookup, including JupyterLab listing/starting a kernel.
findings.concrete_failure: Starting a typo kernel name, or a one-field drift in data/kernels/<name>/kernel.json, tears down the whole Jupyter process. Open notebooks die and the dedicated service must be restarted. This is not filesystem TOCTOU; it is the wrong failure domain for a live request.
findings.repair: Raise jupyter_client.kernelspec.NoSuchKernel (unknown name) or a request-scoped exception (drift). Reserve _fail for pre-start contract failures. Optionally validate all plan kernels once after initialize, before app.start().
findings.acceptance_test: With the server running, get_kernel_spec("nope") and a mutated approved kernel.json argv must return an HTTP/API error while the Jupyter PID stays alive. Startup _fail codes must not run. Restoring the spec allows a later start without restarting the process.

findings.problem: argv and metadata are compared to the approved plan, but any truthy spec.env trips kernel_spec_changed. Approved env is never read. That forbids a normal KernelSpec field and cannot detect env drift versus the plan. Shared process env then becomes the only place for R_HOME/R_LIBS, which is a wrong assumption for local Python and R kernels.
findings.concrete_failure: An approved IRkernel (or Python) spec with env.R_HOME matching the plan still fails on first start because spec.env is truthy. Empty-env-only specs work; any planned non-empty env cannot.
findings.repair: Compare spec.argv, spec.env, and spec.metadata to the approved dict (default env {}). Reject extra/changed keys. Do not treat non-empty env as automatically hostile.
findings.acceptance_test: Approved python3 with env {} matching disk starts. Approved ir with env {R_HOME: <r_home>} matching disk starts. Disk env {R_HOME, EXTRA:1} versus approved {R_HOME} must fail only that start and must not use the _fail startup path.

findings.problem: ServerApp.trust_xheaders is hardcoded True and is omitted from the post-initialize jupyter_security_contract (which does check allow_remote_access, XSRF, unauthenticated access, gateway, and manager types). This process is the Jupyter HTTP listener; HTTPS/WSS termination is an explicit non-claim. Tornado xheaders then trusts client X-Forwarded-For/Proto without a stripping proxy.
findings.concrete_failure: Any TCP client can set X-Forwarded-For and X-Forwarded-Proto before auth. request.remote_ip and request.protocol (kernel WS scheme, secure-request handling) follow the client. This is not shown as a password bypass in the supplied code, and it is not FS TOCTOU.
findings.repair: Default trust_xheaders False. Enable it only when a local proxy is actually stripping/overwriting those headers. Assert not app.trust_xheaders in the security contract unless that proxy mode is on.
findings.acceptance_test: Without a proxy, after initialize the contract must fail if trust_xheaders is True. An unauthenticated request with X-Forwarded-For: 8.8.8.8 and X-Forwarded-Proto: https must leave remote_ip and protocol unaltered by those headers.

limits: HTTPS/WSS, service-account provisioning, startup task, reboot/fresh-login, iPad, and live kernel execution remain release gates and were not treated as implemented.
UI routes, browser wiring, DELIVERABLES.md exact-tab open, verbatim notebook emission, worktree/MAIN durability, and user-account choice were not in the supplied file.
plan builder, plan["environment"] contents, directory layout, and _fail() are unseen; N2 treats _fail as the same abort used for dependencies_missing.
root_dir is a trusted single-user workspace, not an OS sandbox or multitenant boundary.
No live deployment, and root synthetic tests are not a browser proof.
